# Card 208: task-force declaration proposal (objection window 208-taskforce)

Category: task-force declaration. Proposed by: product manager (ready), Claude seat, ctx-1 of card 208.
Probe reference: .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl (16:24 UTC; codex, copilot 16:24:58, grok 16:24:59, agy 16:25:03).
Order: card 208 now runs before card 210 (D160, .mob/records/reranks/2026-10-30-8b.md). Card 210's record checks therefore do not yet apply to 208's records (cost noted in that re-rank note).

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 208 at ready; confirms the F-008 and MD-002 subject tokens (corrective commit), keeps the Done checks within D157, and hands the architect the split question below | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: splits the five runner gaps into one-concern cards (D136) across loop.py, loop_runner.py and facilitator.py, numbers each card's acceptance criteria 1 to 3 before red (D157), and decides the order; the card-record checker requires a slice seat | context: ctx-2
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: turns each slice's ZOMBIES into failing tests, one acceptance criterion per red-green cycle (D157), with injected probe, gh, clock and subprocess fakes, one red test per loophole (D137) | context: ctx-3
- Backend developer [author] (green, refactor): Claude | why: changes the Python tooling in mob-defaults (C:\Users\ringe\mob-crosscli) so each red test passes; the author does not review or QA their own increment | context: ctx-4
- Independent reviewer (audit lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review of each diff against F-008, MD-002 and the audit-15 guardrail F-040, with a runner lens (exit codes, fail-closed gh and probe reads, the repository a command runs in) | context: ctx-5
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: confirms CI, the card record, the probe lines and the F-008 / MD-002 subject tokens before each commit lands; the checker requires a ship seat with its own commit evidence | context: ctx-6
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: a fresh context signs off against the Done checks, because the refinement seat may not hold the second seat | context: ctx-7

Seven seats cover the six roles the card record checker requires (ready, slice, red, green, ship, signoff) plus the independent reviewer. The card already lists the same seven in the same ctx order; this proposal changes only the wording named in the second section. The reviewer seat is named "Independent reviewer (audit lens)", never "auditor": auditor_seated_problems refuses any card seat whose role contains "auditor", because the auditor is external to the mob and never seated.

## Left out
UX designer and frontend developer (no user interface); database developer (no such code); security (no new trust boundary beyond gh reads, which fail closed; the independent reviewer checks that); technical writer (no document); language designer and grammar designer (no language change); performance engineer (no hot path; a probe before each seat is a few calls per card); agile coach (no process change; D145, D157 and D158 are applied, not changed); DevOps / runner expert as a separate seat (see next section).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should a member with different domain knowledge or context join now? Considered carefully, because 208 does touch the loop runner (loop.py, loop_runner.py, facilitator.py card mode), and card 210 left DevOps out on the ground "no runner change". That ground does not carry over here, so the answer is argued afresh. No separate DevOps or runner expert joins now:
- The runner here is Python tooling inside mob-defaults, the same code the architect and backend developer already work in (card 205 changed the neighbouring corrective gate). It is not CI, deployment, a workflow file, a hook or infrastructure, which is what the DevOps role covers.
- The risks specific to a runner (wrong working repository, exit codes, a stale probe, a failing gh call) are exactly the card's Fails-with and ZOMBIES cases, and each is pinned by a red test with fakes. The independent reviewer (audit lens) carries a runner lens, so the author does not review their own reading of those cases.
- Adding a seat now would add a context and a poll without a gap it fills. If a slice needs knowledge none of the seven hold (for example cross-repository git behaviour on Windows in the separate card-repository slice, or how a Decider is invoked for the re-rank), any member adds an expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id). Adding is unchanged by this card.

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 16:24 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota: copilot has_quota=False remaining=-5 (resets 2026-11-01); grok 402 balance exhausted; agy 429 quota reached (resets in about 53h); codex without quota in the same probe set. Each seat is a distinct fresh context (ready ctx-1, slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment. Non-Claude models come first again as soon as a fresh probe shows quota. This is the per-seat Claude reason MD-002 asks for; 208 itself makes that rule checkable by the runner.

## D136 and D157: is the card too large for one card?
Yes. As written it cannot be one red-green run and the architect must split it before red.
- The card already says so itself: Type "the architect splits it, one concern per card, D136", and the Context lists five gaps with a proposed split 208a to 208e.
- It has exactly three Done checks, so it meets the letter of D157 (at most 3), but each check bundles more than one observable behaviour, so "one acceptance criterion per red-green cycle" would still be several cycles hidden in one criterion:
  - Check 1 holds two concerns: parsing role lines only (gap 1) and running in a card repository other than the loop root (gap 2).
  - Check 2 holds three: the Avowry retro, the product manager re-rank through a Decider (gap 3), and probes before every seat (gap 4).
  - Check 3 is one concern (gap 5, reuse of card 205's corrective_gate_message in loop_runner.py).
- Edits span three modules and two actors (a system actor plus a Decider), and cross-repository running is the riskiest change because it moves where every command runs.
- What the architect should consider splitting (the card's order, merge or reorder allowed):
  1. 208a: parse_task_force reads only role lines of the form "- Role: Model | why: ... | context: ctx-N"; Left out, assignee note and domain-expert answer are not roles. Smallest, unblocks card mode for every card. (Check 1, first half.)
  2. 208b: a separate card-repository option, loop root unchanged. (Check 1, second half; own criterion because of its blast radius.)
  3. 208c: reuse card 205's corrective_gate_message in loop_runner.py, failing closed when gh cannot read the issue. Depends on 205 (done), so it may start now; it is the slice that carries the MD-002/F-008 corrective effect on the exit-5 stop. (Check 3.)
  4. 208d: probe before every seat, a probe 60 minutes old or more is refused. (Check 2, third part.)
  5. 208e: Avowry retro and re-rank commands; likely two cards, retro (feedback from every role, each in its own context) then re-rank (through a Decider). The largest; the architect should decide whether the re-rank needs a Decider id interface of its own.
  6. MD-002's two extra requirements (a required reason field per Claude seat in the record, and a pinned probe model) are added "at slice" by the card; they match no existing Done check, so the architect should place them in 208d (probe model) and in a seat-reason slice, or the Done checks gain an uncovered duty. The parent's Done checks bind the sum of the slices; if they exceed three criteria in any one slice, split again.
- Each resulting card keeps at most three Done checks (target one to two), declares its own ZOMBIES, and its red commit body carries "Criterion: n". This task force is proposed for the parent and, unless the architect proposes a different roster for a slice, carries over to each slice with the same ctx roles; a changed roster is a new window.
- D147 on ordering: the slice that reuses 205's gate waited for 205; 205 is done, so no slice is now blocked on it.

## D157 applies
One acceptance criterion per red-green cycle, checked from git (5-card experiment, Decider D157):
- The slice (architect, ctx-2) numbers each resulting card's criteria 1 to 3 before any red.
- Each red commit body carries "Criterion: n".
- The green for criterion n lands before any red for n+1.
- Greens are pushed at once.
- ZOMBIES already in the card are implemented by QA, not rewritten (a ZOMBIES change is a card-text fix through this window).
- Each commit stays within D136, cites F-008 (and MD-002 where it applies) in the subject (corrective commit), references D145 and D136, red first (D137).

## D158 applies
The facilitator's pre-window checklist (D158) is run before this window opens: the proposal names seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff; the reviewer seat is not named auditor; the roster is not template boilerplate; every seat has a domain/why and a distinct context; the Claude reason cites a probe file and time; the card text lines match the proposal (second section below); every declared role is listed for polling (checklist file to be committed before the window, as for window 210-taskforce).

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer (ready ctx-1 is the proposer; slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), each in its own fresh context. A declared role that is not polled makes the window invalid.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition per objection (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Card-text changes proposed with this declaration are card-text fixes in the same window (D153 L1).

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card (and can be re-declared by another window); nothing is published, deleted or migrated, and the roster can be changed by a Decider mid-card. It applies Task-Force Driven Development, D136, D145, D157 and D158 as written and changes no agreement, D-record or checker. (The card itself changes the runner, but that is the card's work under its own Done checks, not this declaration.) The architect's split creates cards under existing rules; it does not change the card process. F-008 and MD-002 stay open until the corrective slices land; D147 allows the start because the issue names them.
